newsitem.title: UK: S&P raises snr debt of Ciba-Geigy to AAA from AA.
newsitem.headline: S&P raises snr debt of Ciba-Geigy to AAA from AA.

text.p: LONDON, Dec 18 (Reuter - Standard and Poor's said on Wednesday it raised its senior debt ratings of Ciba-Geigy Ltd. and related entities to AAA from AA and said the outlook was stable.

S&P said in a statement it removed the companies from CreditWatch, where they were placed with positive implications on March 7, 1996 following announcement of a merger agreement between Ciba and Sandoz Ltd.
The S&P statement continued:

Standard & Poor's indicated in its September 10, 1996 press release that ratings will be upgraded upon U.S. approval for the merger. Yesterday, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission approved the transaction, which is structured as a merger of equals based on an exchange of shares. The upgrade to AAA reflects an improvement in the combined group's business position in conjunction with the conservative financing of the transaction giving the new group one of the best financial profiles in the pharmaceutical industry.

Ratings are based on the credit quality of a newly created company, Novartis Ltd., which will absorb the rated entities, Sandoz and Ciba. The merger was approved by each group's shareholders on April 23 and 24, 1996, and approval from the European Commission was granted on July 17, 1996. Conditions imposed by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (divestments in crop protection and animal health as well as offering third parties access to technology) do not materially affect the overall transaction or the combined group's business position.

As regards the groups' disposals of chemicals businesses, Sandoz announced the disposal of its construction chemicals unit for Swiss franc (SFr) 1.3 billion to SKW Trostberg in late August 1996, and Ciba reported in its interim results for 1996 that shares in the new specialty chemicals company will be transferred to shareholders prior but no later than the 1997 ordinary general meeting.
From a business risk perspective the merger:

-- combines 2 superior players in industries with generally favorable risk characteristics (as evidenced by both Ciba and Sandoz individually already holding Standard & Poor's highest commercial paper rating, A1 plus, prior to the transaction);

-- gives the group leading positions globally in pharmaceuticals (no. 2), self-medication (no. 7), optics (no. 2), opthalmics (no.5), medical nutrition (no.2) and in agrochemicals (no. 1 in crop protection, no. 2 in seeds), thus making the combined entity the no. 1 player in life sciences;

-- improves Novartis's health care business position via a larger portfolio of ethical drugs and self-medication products, a better therapeutic coverage, and improved critical mass in terms of marketing and R&D effort.

Thus, Novartis will be better prepared to meet the challenges, such as healthcare reforms, facing the pharmaceuticals industry. The other business areas of Novartis all enjoy leading positions, and have synergies with healthcare. The disposal of the chemical units will also make the combined entity less cyclical than previously.

From a financial risk perspective, in contrast to most mergers in the industry with the exception of Pharmacia AB's merger with The Upjohn Company, the conservative all paper financing of the transaction does not impair the combined group's already strong financial posture. The combination will have less debt than cash (SFr3.6 billion net cash at year-end 1995 on a pro-forma basis).
OUTLOOK: Stable.

The group's leading business positions in conjunction with its superior cash-generating ability and financial posture, continuation of a conservative track record regarding financial policies, merger synergies and cost-cutting potential, and financial flexibility stemming from asset disposals should enable the group to maintain its superior ratings, despite its role as a consolidator in a still fragmented industry. Conversely, material changes in financial policies or its financial posture, although not anticipated, would put pressure on the ratings, Standard & Poor's said.
